assignment_rule.policy: Highest-scoring candidate at or above 0.75 wins. A story with no candidate at or above 0.75 is recorded as a routing gap and left UNASSIGNED - never force-assigned to the best of a bad set.
assignment_rule.agent_existence_rule: Every agent named here was verified to exist at claude-global-library/agents/{name}/agent.md in this session.

trigger_criteria: Story touches the storage-adapter (ZoneRepository port) interface
p1_security_override.effect: A mandatory security review gate is attached to the story. The reviewing agent is distinct from the implementing agent (Maker-Checker). The story cannot close on the implementing agent's report alone.
p1_security_override.deviation_note: DASH-STORY-007 was NOT in the brief's expected list, but its AC-014 is verbatim cross-tenant isolation ('returns results only from tenant A's physically partitioned collection, UserAffinity never acts as a tenant-isolation term, no shared cache key leaks a hit/miss signal'), and HLD ADR-013 plus threats I-1/I-2/I-3 make it the highest cross-tenant risk surface in Sprint 1. The stated criteria were applied literally rather than the parenthetical enumeration. This deviation is surfaced for user decision, not silently adopted.

assignments.rationale: HLD Section 6 names the Orchestrator a Facade and the context assembler a Builder over a greedy 0/1-knapsack (Section 5); HLD Section 2 locks the surface to Python 3.12 + gRPC/FastAPI. python-backend-engineer's mandatory skills (python-core, python-design-patterns-core, fastapi-core, dsa-core, api-design-core) cover all four of those simultaneously, which no other verified candidate does. Ownership check against HLD 3.1 passes: the Orchestrator owns no persistent data, so this is an application-layer assignment with no storage-tier claim.

must_not_deviate: ADR-005 storage choice (in-process LRU Shape A, Redis Shape B)
O(1) get/put/evict class
TTL-primary eviction, not score-primary
No mutation of any other zone as a side effect (AC-001)
tenant_id mandatory at the ZoneRepository port signature (HLD 3.0 invariant 2)
assignments.p1_trigger_evaluation: Implements a zone adapter, but the storage-adapter INTERFACE (the ZoneRepository port contract itself, FR-011) is defined in DASH-STORY-001 and not modified here. Advisory: if this story ends up amending the port signature, the P1 trigger fires retroactively and this assignment must be re-gated.
assignments.logging_note: Cite as AR1-002. Fallback candidate database-engineer recorded at 0.7945 - above threshold, so a reassignment does not require a new AR.0 pass.

assignments.title: Episodic Memory zone (Zone 2) - chronological recency store
assignments.rationale: HLD Section 5 states this zone's entire design as an index and pagination decision: append-only table, B-tree PK on (tenant, session, seq), BRIN on occurred_at (chosen because it is ~1000x smaller than B-tree for naturally-ordered timestamps), and keyset pagination at O(1) per page versus offset's O(offset). Those are schema/index judgments, which is database-engineer's declared surface (rdbms-core, performance-optimization). Assigning this to the backend agent would put the BRIN-vs-B-tree and keyset-vs-offset calls in the hands of an agent without indexing depth.
must_not_deviate: BRIN on occurred_at, B-tree PK on (tenant, session, seq)
Keyset pagination, never OFFSET
Per-entry decay attribute exposed in the query result (AC-002)
Append-only
tenant_id in every query
assignments.p1_trigger_evaluation: Not a P1 trigger under the three stated criteria. However AC-002-DPDP-1 imposes a DPDP Act 2023 erasure-locatability obligation on PII-bearing conversational content. Recorded as a P2 privacy-advisory consult (see routing_gaps AR1-G3) rather than promoted to P1 - promoting it would be an invented criterion.
assignments.logging_note: Cite as AR1-003. This is the only story where the top candidate is NOT python-backend-engineer by a margin wider than 0.10, making it the clearest hand-off boundary in the sprint.

assignments.title: Zone 2 capacity cap and MaxAge forced-archival backstop (OAQ-4)
assignments.rationale: The backstop is a rotation-worker sweep that ranks by MemoryScore and applies an operator-configurable cap and MaxAge (NFR-009). Its centre of gravity is the sweep + config surface + MemoryScore consumption (Template Method, HLD Section 6), not the DELETE. The 0.0735 margin is the narrowest in the sprint, so database-engineer is recorded as a genuine co-owner candidate for the bulk-delete and index-impact portion; a split is defensible if AR.2 finds this story on the critical path.

must_not_deviate: Cap and MaxAge are deployment config, read per sweep run, no code change (AC-002-CAP-2)
Eviction ordering is lowest-MemoryScore-first
No attempt at an Archived transition - there is no destination in Sprint 1 (HLD 12F)
Eviction must satisfy, not bypass, a pending DPDP erasure obligation (AC-002-CAP-DPDP-1)

That is a cross-zone consistency property with a privacy failure mode.

assignments.logging_note: Cite as AR1-004. Narrowest margin in the sprint (0.0735) - flagged for AR.2 re-examination if this story becomes a bottleneck.

assignments.title: Provenance/Audit zone (Zone 7) - source, confidence, edit history
assignments.rationale: The story's binding constraints are database-level: an append-only table with NO UPDATE grant for any service role, a SHA-256 prev_hash chain for tamper evidence, and per-service role least privilege (HLD 3.8, Section 10 threat R-1, ADR-010). database-engineer carries rdbms-core plus application-security-core, which is the pairing this needs. python-backend-engineer clears the threshold at 0.783 and is the correct co-owner for the confidence-computation formula (source_type base values, the -0.3 disputed modifier, the x0.9 per compression generation) if the work is split.
assignments.hld_ownership_crosscheck: MATCH - HLD 3.8 / ADR-010 / Section 5 (hash chain) / Section 10 (R-1)
must_not_deviate: No UPDATE grant exists on the Zone 7 table for any service role - corrections are new chained records
SHA-256 prev_hash -> record_hash chain
Confidence is COMPUTED from source_type and modifiers, never assigned once (HLD 3.8)
Append-only, O(1) amortized write
assignments.p1_trigger_evaluation: TRIGGERED - this IS Zone 7 (Provenance). It is also the design's stated strongest memory-poisoning control (HLD T-1) and the anti-hallucination backbone, so a review miss here is the highest-consequence defect available in Sprint 1.

p1_reviewer.review_scope: Verify hash-chain tamper-detectability against HLD threat R-1, verify the absence of an UPDATE grant is enforced by DB role rather than by application convention (threat T-2), and verify least privilege on every per-service role touching the table. Skills cryptography-core + application-security-core + security-governance-compliance apply.
p1_reviewer.maker_checker: Reviewer is distinct from implementer (database-engineer). Story cannot close on the implementer's report alone.

assignments.logging_note: Cite as AR1-005. Highest-consequence P1 in the sprint per HLD T-1.

assignments.title: Cross-cutting provenance write-path enforcement (WAL/outbox gate)
assignments.rationale: The gate lives on the Orchestrator's write path (HLD 7.2), rejects with HTTP 422, and is backed by a Transactional Outbox / WAL durability barrier (ADR-010, HLD Section 6). python-backend-engineer's fastapi-core covers the 422 contract, message-queues-core covers the outbox and relay, and it already owns the write path from DASH-STORY-001 - which matters because AC-016 requires the gate be structurally unbypassable rather than a per-call convention, and structural unbypassability is easiest to guarantee inside the component that owns the path.
assignments.hld_ownership_crosscheck: MATCH - HLD 7.2 write path / ADR-010 / Section 6 (Transactional Outbox)
must_not_deviate: 422 on unresolvable source_type, rejected BEFORE persistence (AC-010, AC-016)
WAL/outbox durability barrier - Zone 7 must not be a synchronous SPOF (ADR-010)
Structurally unbypassable, not a convention
Applies across ALL Sprint 1 zones, not per-zone opt-in
assignments.p1_trigger_evaluation: TRIGGERED - this is the enforcement path INTO Zone 7 and the product's entire anti-hallucination thesis (WSJF rank 2, Must-Be Kano). A bypass here silently voids DASH-STORY-005's guarantees.

p1_reviewer.review_scope: Adversarially test that no write path reaches persistence without a resolvable source_type - including malformed, partially-valid, and replayed requests. assignments.title: Retrieval-Index zone (Zone 6) - hybrid vector + lexical index
assignments.rationale: This is the one story whose decisive content is retrieval-system expertise rather than service or schema work: HNSW parameterization (M=16, efConstruction=200, efSearch=64), BM25 over OpenSearch, and RRF fusion at score = sum_r 1/(60 + rank_r(d)) chosen specifically to avoid cross-scale score mixing (ADR-007, ADR-008, Section 5). ai-engineer is the only verified candidate carrying vector-database-core AND rag-core. Notably the runner-up falls BELOW threshold at 0.680 - there is no second valid assignment here, which makes this story a single-agent dependency.
must_not_deviate: Per-tenant PHYSICAL partitioning - one Qdrant collection and one OpenSearch index per tenant (ADR-007, ADR-013)
UserAffinity is never a tenant-isolation term (AC-014, ADR-013)
Cache keys are tenant_id-prefixed - no shared key may leak a hit/miss oracle (AC-014)
RRF fusion, not score normalization across scales (ADR-008)
Zone 1 is deliberately NOT indexed (HLD 3.7, AC-006 as corrected)
assignments.p1_trigger_evaluation: TRIGGERED on the cross-tenant-isolation criterion. AC-014 is a verbatim cross-tenant isolation requirement and HLD ADR-013 makes tenant isolation a hard physical partition with threats I-1/I-2/I-3. This story was not in the brief's parenthetical list; see p1_security_override.deviation_note.

p1_reviewer.review_scope: BOLA/IDOR-class testing across tenant boundaries on the retrieval path, plus cache-oracle probing (does a tenant B hit measurably change tenant A's latency or response?). OWASP API Top 10 2023 BOLA is a P1 hard-fail for this reviewer. Verify the partition is physical, not a WHERE clause.
p1_reviewer.maker_checker: Reviewer is distinct from implementer (ai-engineer). Story cannot close on the implementer's report alone.
p1_reviewer.conditional: Applies only if the user accepts the P1 scope extension in p1_security_override.deviation_note. If rejected, this reverts to a standard peer review and the sprint's highest-rated cross-tenant risk goes ungated.

mathematical_delegation.trigger: AC-006-COST-1 requires a reported average cost per retrieval query (C_fixed_vector + C_fixed_lexical + c_var*V)/V AND a separately reported marginal cost c_var.
mathematical_delegation.why_blocking: The AC explicitly forbids presenting average cost alone as an efficiency indicator, because at Sprint 1 volumes it is dominated by fixed-capacity amortization. Self-deriving this is exactly the approximation the orchestrator is forbidden to make.
mathematical_delegation.position: Blocking dependency - the cost figures must return before the story's cost estimate is produced.

assignments.title: Memory Score computation engine (six-term formula)
assignments.rationale: HLD Section 5 reduces the scoring service to a fixed 6-element vector, an O(1) dot product, and an exp(-lambda*dt) decay; Section 6 makes MemoryScore an immutable Value Object so the six terms are safely cacheable and score:explain is trivially reproducible. That is Python design-pattern and config-surface work, which python-backend-engineer owns. The formula's derivations are delegated, not self-derived.
assignments.hld_ownership_crosscheck: MATCH - HLD 3.1 (scoring service) / Sections 12A-12C / Section 6 (Value Object)
must_not_deviate: All six terms normalized to [0,1] before weighting
MemoryScore and ScoreTerms are immutable Value Objects - compared, never mutated
Default weight profile 1/6 each, but operator-overridable without a code change (AC-017, NFR-009)
Importance is explicit-tag-only, defaulting to 0.5 (AC-012-SCORE-1, HLD 12F) - Zone 4 inference is out of Sprint 1 scope
assignments.p1_trigger_evaluation: No Zone 7 write surface, no storage adapter, no tenant-isolation logic. ADR-013's rule that UserAffinity must never act as a tenant-isolation term is consumed here but enforced in DASH-STORY-007; recorded as a cross-story invariant to verify at the integration gate.

mathematical_delegation.trigger: Normalization of all six terms to [0,1], the structural score-floor implications named in OAQ-3, and the exponential-decay half-life-to-lambda conversion.
mathematical_delegation.why_blocking: OAQ-3's score floor is a structural property of the weighted sum - if six terms each floor above zero, the composite can never cross ArchiveThreshold, which would silently break DASH-STORY-009's rotation. This must be derived, not assumed.
mathematical_delegation.position: Blocking dependency - must return before the weight/threshold configuration surface is finalized.

assignments.title: Rotation state machine - Active to Compressed (Archived deferred)
assignments.rationale: HLD Section 6 names this a State Machine with guarded transitions and a Template Method sweep skeleton, precisely because the Phase 0 review's own bug (a fast-decaying item skipping compression) came from treating the lifecycle as score bands instead of states. Section 5 specifies a per-zone hierarchical timer wheel (bucketed min-heap) with an O(1) closed-form deadline and an O(k log N) sweep. python-design-patterns-core and dsa-core cover both halves.

O(k log N) sweep, not an O(N) scan

mathematical_delegation.trigger: The closed-form deadline delta_t* = -(1/lambda) ln(6*theta - C) and the O(k log N) sweep bound (HLD Section 12C).
mathematical_delegation.why_blocking: The closed form is what replaces an infeasible O(N)-per-sweep scan. An error in it produces wrong rotation times rather than a crash - a silent-failure class.
mathematical_delegation.position: Blocking dependency - must return before the timer-wheel implementation is written.

assignments.title: ADR-012 deadline-invalidation wiring on non-Recency term mutation
assignments.rationale: The three mutation paths this story must wire (Frequency-on-access via the DASH-STORY-001 read path, ProvenanceConfidence-on-conflict via DASH-STORY-005/006, Importance-on-override via DASH-STORY-008) are already owned by python-backend-engineer in 001, 006 and 008. Assigning this elsewhere would create three cross-agent handoffs on a story whose stated failure mode is a SILENT correctness bug (stale rotation deadlines), i.e. the failure most likely to survive a handoff undetected. Same-agent ownership is the risk control here, not a convenience.
must_not_deviate: ALL THREE mutation paths must be wired, not a subset (HLD 12C: 'must be wired into every term-mutation path')
O(log N) re-insert bound
No rotation decision may ever act on a stale deadline (AC-012-INVAL-1)
Do not re-implement the sweep itself - that is DASH-STORY-009

dependency_integrity_check.method: error-handling-patterns - traverse backlog_draft.json dependency_graph for cycles and for assignment-induced deadlocks before any agent is dispatched.
dependency_integrity_check.cycle_detection: PASS - no cycle. Every edge points from a later story to a strictly earlier-resolvable one. Longest chain: 001 -> 002 -> 005 -> 006 (depth 4) and 001 -> 003 -> 007 -> 008 -> 004 (depth 5).
dependency_integrity_check.assignment_induced_deadlock: NONE. No two stories are mutually blocked by holding each other's assigned agent. python-backend-engineer's 7 stories are all on a consistent topological order (001, 002, 006, 008, 009, 010 sequential-compatible; 004 after 008).
dependency_integrity_check.serialization_warning: python-backend-engineer holds 7 of 10 stories (37 of 55 story points). Under strictly sequential single-agent execution the sprint's critical path is agent-bound, not dependency-bound. The dependency DAG permits DASH-STORY-003 (database-engineer) and DASH-STORY-007 (ai-engineer) to run in parallel with the python-backend-engineer chain; AR.2 must exploit that or the sprint serializes. This is a system-design bottleneck finding, not a reassignment trigger.

routing_gaps.gap: Single valid agent. ai-engineer scores 0.889; the next candidate (python-backend-engineer, 0.680) falls below the 0.75 threshold, as do ml-engineer (0.5815) and data-engineer (0.533). There is no compliant fallback if ai-engineer is unavailable.
routing_gaps.why_not_force_assigned: python-backend-engineer at 0.680 would be a force-assignment below threshold. Per the stated constraint, it is surfaced rather than adopted.
routing_gaps.recommended_action: Either accept the single-agent risk on the sprint's largest story (8 SP), or pair ai-engineer (HNSW/BM25/RRF decisions) with python-backend-engineer (adapter + cache-key plumbing) as an explicit two-agent split with a signed interface contract. A split does not require either agent to clear 0.75 alone on the whole story - only on its own slice.

routing_gaps.gap: No agent in claude-global-library specializes in application-level pluggable storage-adapter/repository-port design as a first-class concern. The nearest-named agent, database-storage-engineer, is scoped to a database's OWN storage engine internals (WAL/ARIES recovery, LSM-tree, B+tree, MVCC, buffer-pool policy) and scores 0.2875 here.

Extend that same reviewer as a non-blocking privacy consult on DASH-STORY-003. If the user wants DPDP erasure implemented as its own capability rather than reviewed, it needs a new backlog story - it is not implicitly covered by any Sprint 1 assignment.
